# Test Suite Index

14 files: 14 test suites holding 123 `[test]` functions, 0 compile-fail fixtures, 0 scripts. How a test tree is laid out and what each class of file is: `tests/ARCHITECTURE.md` at the repo root.

## boulder-dash/

### test_cave.das

Cave simulation: physics, creatures, input, and couplings.

- `test_ascii_roundtrip` - An ASCII cave parses to the right size and Rockford position and prints back to the same text.
- `test_boulder_falls_into_empty` - A boulder over an empty cell moves down one cell as a falling boulder, then settles on the next tick.
- `test_stacked_boulders_one_cell_per_tick` - A stack of boulders falls one cell per tick: the scan bit stops the lower boulder from falling twice in one tick.
- `test_boulder_rests_on_dirt` - Dirt is not empty space: a boulder on dirt does not move.
- `test_boulder_rolls_left` - A boulder resting on another boulder rolls off diagonally to the left when the left side is free.
- `test_boulder_prefers_left_over_right` - When both sides are free, a rolling boulder goes left and not right.
- `test_falling_crushes_rockford` - A falling boulder that lands on Rockford kills him and sets the died event.
- `test_stationary_boulder_does_not_crush` - A boulder already resting on Rockford's head does not kill him; both stay in place.
- `test_collect_diamond_and_grab` - Walking onto a diamond collects it, and a grab clears dirt or collects a diamond while Rockford stays in place.
- `test_diamond_fall_events` - A diamond fires the fell event when it starts falling and the landed event, not before, when it comes to rest.
- `test_peek_step` - The step preview predicts a move into dirt, and predicts no move into steel or into a boulder.
- `test_input_latch` - The input latch keeps a tapped direction through a later idle latch, lets the last tap win, holds a locked direction, and queues a changed tap for the tick after consume.
- `test_push` - Pushing a boulder sideways takes a wind-up tick and then moves both; a push into an occupied cell or upward does nothing.
- `test_firefly_left_hand` - A firefly follows the left-hand rule: with left and up blocked it turns east and moves.
- `test_butterfly_mirror` - A butterfly follows the mirrored right-hand rule: with east blocked it turns west into the empty cell.
- `test_explosion_firefly_and_butterfly` - A falling boulder on a firefly leaves a 3x3 empty blast, while a butterfly hit by a boulder or touched by amoeba blasts into diamonds; steel survives.
- `test_amoeba` - Enclosed amoeba turns into diamonds, amoeba grows into dirt, and an amoeba mass that fills the cave turns into boulders.
- `test_magic_wall` - A falling boulder activates a magic wall and comes out below it as a falling diamond.
- `test_magic_expires_to_brick` - An active magic wall runs out after its time limit, sets the spent event, and turns into brick.
- `test_expanding_wall` - An expanding wall grows left first, one cell per tick, and keeps its origin cell.
- `test_slime_lets_boulder_through` - Fully permeable slime lets a boulder pass through it and stays in place.
- `test_quota_exit_and_timeout` - Reaching the diamond quota opens the exit and walking into it clears the cave; running out of time kills Rockford.
- `test_magic_wall_falling_gate` - A magic wall converts only a falling boulder: a resting boulder stays on top, and a spent wall stops a falling one.
- `test_tile_enum_coupling` - The Tile enum, its glyph table, its family range tests and the insect heading encoding agree member for member.
- `test_peek_step_parity` - For every tile in Rockford's path, the step preview agrees with the tick: a predicted step always lands, and an unpredicted step never happens.
- `test_ascii_cave_exit_contract` - A raw ASCII cave has no diamond quota, so its exit never opens; finish_cave sets the quota and the exit then opens.

### test_generate.das

- `test_generated_cave_invariants` - A generated cave has the standard size, a steel border, one Rockford, an exit, diamonds with a quota no larger than the diamonds present, enough time, and scattered boulders.
- `test_same_seed_identical` - Generation is deterministic: the same world seed and cave index give the same layout and quota.
- `test_different_seeds_differ` - Changing either the world seed or the cave index changes the generated layout.
- `test_fallback_playable` - The fallback cave passes the sanity check, has a steel border, and holds exactly one Rockford.
- `test_many_seeds_sane` - Caves from 20 seeds all pass the sanity check, and none asks for more diamonds than it holds.
- `test_spawn_not_sucker` - In early caves across many seeds, a Rockford who does not move survives the first 24 ticks: nothing crushes or catches him at the spawn.

### uncategorized.das

- `test_sweep_endpoints_are_what_is_heard` - The pitch heard in a synthesized sweep, counted by zero crossings, matches the frequency its endpoints name, and a constant tone stays at its named pitch.
- `test_bank_remap_preserves_audio` - The legacy sweep formula over (fs, fe) and the corrected gen_sine_sweep over (fs, 2*fe - fs) give the same samples, so remapping the effect endpoints left every effect sounding as before.

## latchpoint/

### test_ambient.das

Ambient life: robot activity, chatter, sound, and scenery.

- `test_robot_activity` - The drill sparks only while spinning at full extension against the plate, stays clear of the track, and stops while its robot listens; Patch's work lamp follows its schedule and his listening without ever turning his eyes off.
- `test_chatter_guards` - Background chatter cannot run a tool call or change the game, is dropped when the player is busy, takes a turn, changes the world, walks away, disables it or lets it expire, and queues its audio without replacing the player's conversation.
- `test_feedback_and_sound` - Music ducking combines capture and speech into one target, mechanical loops stay bounded with silent seams, the robot indicator is brighter listening than thinking and follows the speech level, robot lamps sit at their animation attachment, and background rocks stay outside the playable yard.
- `test_finishing_materials` - Robot voice processing colors each resident's voice slightly, stays within range and leaves the samples untouched when switched off, and outcrop meshes stay in their unit box with unit normals.

### test_controls.das

Player controls: pointer, keys, menu, chat, shutdown save.

- `test_pointer_and_retina` - Either drag button drags the camera, and the UI scissor rectangle scales to the framebuffer and flips to the bottom-left origin on a retina display as on a 1:1 one.
- `test_navigation` - Menu clicks hit only the visible buttons, arrows and WASD move the same way, and a doubled key never speeds up the normalized movement.
- `test_lifecycle_guards` - Closing the game from the untouched opening menu leaves the saved pose byte for byte, while closing during play saves the current pose.
- `test_chat_activation` - Both Enter keys confirm a chat edit, a held key does not toggle a setting again, and the key that opens chat swallows its own character but not the next one typed.

### test_native_async.das

- `test_cancelled_response` - A response that arrives after its request was cancelled is drained without applying the action it proposes.
- `test_busy_input` - A silent recording is rejected before recognition starts, and retrying a typed message while the old request still drains keeps the typed text.
- `test_empty_recognition` - A recognition result of only whitespace ends the turn as failed without opening the text editor.
- `test_finished_job_can_be_released_at_shutdown` - Shutdown releases a finished inference job and clears its handles, and a minimized framebuffer is not drawn while a visible one is.
- `test_pending_job_is_handed_to_nonblocking_reaper` - Shutdown hands a still-running inference job to the reaper and returns at once instead of waiting for the request to time out.
- `test_minimized_frame_drains_without_launching_ambient_followup` - A chatter reply finished on a minimized frame clears the chatter stage without starting speech synthesis.

### test_runtime.das

Native runtime: authority, routes, saves, gates, archive.

- `test_native_runtime` - Only the resident with the authority opens each gate; the power-first route needs the accepted task and both archive conditions, the repair-first route uses each item once, and neither a free spare nor a follow request duplicates an item or skips the repair.
- `test_native_save_and_motion` - A runtime snapshot round-trips the inventory and each resident's own memory, a partial or wrong-version save is rejected without touching the current world, and an opening gate keeps blocking until it gives head clearance.
- `test_archive_payoff` - The archive record can be inspected only once the archive is open, records its event once, survives a save round trip, and is offered only to an avatar standing at it.

### test_save_recovery.das

- `test_new_game_replaces_a_corrupt_save` - New Game over a corrupt save writes a fresh valid save, keeps the corrupt one as .corrupt, and writes its pose beside the chosen save without touching the normal pose save.
- `test_save_recovery_and_missing_save` - A broken or missing primary save is recovered from the previous save and republished, the broken file is kept as .corrupt, and a missing save with no backup starts a writable runtime.
- `test_new_game_rolls_back_when_publish_fails` - When New Game cannot write its save, the previous world is restored and the player is told.

### test_shading.das

- `test_camera_and_normals` - The HDR check rejects pixels past half-float range, sky interpolation keeps the center ray pointing forward, and stretched surfaces light with inverse-transpose normals.
- `test_twilight` - The surface shader samples the sky cubemap with explicit LOD, storm flashes stay bounded and rare and turn off for reduced flashes, the hanging lamp swings on its tether, and the yard lights follow Patch's heading and the generator power.
- `test_beveled_geometry` - A beveled box has unit normals, outward-facing triangles and exact bounds, a zero bevel gives a plain 24-vertex box, and an oversized radius still gives unit normals.

### test_world.das

The yard: props, collision, Patch, generator, telemetry.

- `test_prop_placement` - The actuator rests on top of its crate, the rotated salvage crates are spaced so their tops never overlap, and the generator's collider draws no wall.
- `test_yard` - Continue restores a valid saved pose and rejects invalid ones, residents and walls block the avatar without tunneling, the gates switch collision, pickups need proximity and vanish once taken, and Patch follows only when he agreed and is repaired.
- `test_patch_facing` - A following Patch turns toward his travel no faster than his turn rate and stops dead when told, and his model's eyes turn with his body heading.
- `test_generator_coil` - Installing the coil does not start the generator: the manual starter needs unbroken work, a repaired following Patch walks to the clutch and speeds it up, and nobody starts it without the coil or from far away.
- `test_scene_snapshot` - Reading the live scene telemetry twice reports the world state each time without changing it.

### uncategorized_persistent_heap_stack_262144.das

- `test_core_profile_cleanup` - In a strict core-profile OpenGL context, the fixed-function cleanup and a font draw with its cleanup leave no GL error while VAO zero is bound.

## sequence/

### test_anim.das

- `test_chip_place_scale` - The chip-place scale curve starts at 0, rises to a 1.2 overshoot at t=0.6, settles back to 1.0 at t=1, and clamps past the end.
- `test_chip_remove_scale` - The chip-remove scale curve starts at 1.0, flashes up to 1.3 at t=0.2, shrinks to 0 at t=1, and never goes negative.
- `test_chip_remove_alpha` - The chip-remove fade goes from opaque to transparent without ever rising, and clamps outside 0..1.
- `test_card_fly_ease` - The card-fly ease-out runs from 0 to 1 without ever falling and covers more distance in its first half than in its second.

### test_bots.das

- `test_bot_random_returns_legal_move` - The random bot finds a legal move for either player on a fresh deal.
- `test_bot_random_different_seeds` - The random bot's seed changes its choice: some seed picks a different cell than seed 1.
- `test_bot_random_handles_jacks` - Holding only a red jack, the random bot plays it on an empty cell; holding only a black jack, it plays a legal removal of an opponent chip.
- `test_bot_random_no_moves` - With an empty hand the random bot returns the no-move answer, card index -1.
- `test_bot_random_many_moves_all_legal` - Every move the random bot makes over 100 turns of one game is legal.
- `test_bot_random_full_game` - Two random bots play a game for up to 500 moves without getting stuck before the first move.
- `test_bot_greedy_returns_legal_move` - The greedy bot finds a legal move on a fresh deal.
- `test_bot_greedy_full_game` - Two greedy bots play a game for up to 500 moves without getting stuck before the first move.
- `test_bot_lookahead_returns_legal_move` - The lookahead bot finds a legal move for either player on a fresh deal.
- `test_bot_lookahead_depth1_like_greedy` - Lookahead at depth 1 picks the same cell as the greedy bot.
- `test_bot_lookahead_no_moves` - With an empty hand the lookahead bot returns the no-move answer, card index -1.
- `test_bot_lookahead_many_moves_all_legal` - Every move the lookahead bot makes over 100 turns of one game is legal.
- `test_bot_lookahead_full_game` - Two lookahead bots play a game for up to 500 moves without getting stuck before the first move.
- `test_bot_lookahead_depth3` - Lookahead at depth 3 still returns a legal move.
- `test_bot_lookahead_jack_lookahead_zero` - With jack_lookahead = 0, so the inner search skips jacks, the lookahead bot still returns a legal move.

### test_gameplay.das

- `test_board_dimensions` - The board is 10 by 10, 100 cells.
- `test_free_corners` - The four corners are FREE spaces and is_corner is true for them and false elsewhere.
- `test_exactly_96_non_free_cells` - Exactly 96 board cells are not FREE.
- `test_each_card_appears_twice` - The board shows 48 distinct cards and each appears exactly twice.
- `test_no_jacks_on_board` - No board cell shows a jack.
- `test_all_board_cards_valid` - Every cell except the corners shows a card.
- `test_jack_helpers` - Spades and clubs jacks are black removers, hearts and diamonds jacks are red wilds, and is_jack is true for all four and no other card.
- `test_board_card_bounds` - board_card answers no card outside the 10x10 board and club_1 at row 0, column 1.
- `test_card_to_string` - card_to_string gives the enum name of a card and an empty string for no card.
- `test_card_suit_rank_idx` - Suit and rank indices count clubs 0 through spades 3 and ace 0 through king 12.
- `test_chip_placement` - A placed chip reads back and can be overwritten, clearing restores no chip, and reads or places outside the board answer none or false.
- `test_chip_color_cycle` - next_chip_color cycles none, blue, green, red, yellow and back to none.
- `test_chip_colors_have_alpha` - Every chip color converts to a visible color with nonzero alpha.
- `test_double_deck` - The double deck holds 104 cards: each of the 52 cards twice.
- `test_make_game_hand_sizes` - A new game deals 7 cards each to 2 players, 6 to 3 players and 5 to 4 players.
- `test_make_game_draw_pile` - After the deal the draw pile holds the rest of the 104 cards: 90 for 2 players and 84 for 4.
- `test_make_game_state` - A new game starts in the playing phase with player 0 to move and no winner.
- `test_all_dealt_cards_valid` - Every card dealt to four players is a real card.
- `test_shuffle_is_deterministic` - The same shuffle seed deals the same first card.
- `test_shuffle_different_seeds` - Two different shuffle seeds deal player 0 a different hand.
- `test_card_suit_rank` - Suit and rank indices are right for a queen, a ten and an ace: ranks count from ace 0, so the ten is 9.
- `test_sort_hand` - sort_hand orders a hand by card enum value, suit first then rank.
- `test_legal_moves_normal_card` - Every legal move for a non-jack card targets an empty cell that shows that same card.
- `test_apply_move` - Applying a legal move puts the mover's chip on the cell, unless the card is a black jack, and passes the turn to the next player.
- `test_apply_move_wrong_player` - A move applied for a player whose turn it is not is refused.
- `test_dead_card_detection` - A card is dead only when both of its board cells are taken.
- `test_jacks_never_dead` - A jack is never a dead card.
- `test_player_chip_colors` - Players 0 to 3 play blue, green, red and yellow chips.
- `test_full_game_simulation` - A two-player game played from the legal move list runs for up to 200 turns without getting stuck before the first turn.
- `test_is_legal_move` - Every move from legal_moves passes is_legal_move, while a normal card on a cell showing another card, a move off the board, and a normal card on a taken cell are all illegal.
- `test_horizontal_sequence` - Five chips of one color in a row are found as a sequence.
- `test_vertical_sequence` - Five chips of one color in a column are found as a sequence.
- `test_diagonal_sequence` - Five chips of one color on a down-right diagonal are found as a sequence.
- `test_anti_diagonal_sequence` - Five chips of one color on a down-left diagonal are found as a sequence.
- `test_free_corner_in_sequence` - A FREE corner counts as a chip of any color: four chips next to it complete a sequence for blue and for green.
- `test_no_sequence_with_4` - Four chips in a row are not a sequence.
- `test_overlapping_sequences_share_one_cell` - Nine chips in a row form two sequences, which share one cell.
- `test_win_condition_2_players` - With two players the winner needs two sequences: one is not a win and a second one wins for player 0.
- `test_win_condition_3_players` - With three players one sequence wins: a green sequence wins for player 1.
- `test_black_jack_cant_remove_from_sequence` - A chip that is part of a finished sequence cannot be removed.
- `test_apply_move_triggers_win` - The move that completes a winning sequence ends the game with the mover as the winner.
